Uganda content gap analysis · cycle 2026-09

OpenStreetMap has mapped a Uganda that Wikimedia has never described

OSM carries 93,272 named Ugandan features across 12 classes of thing: villages, schools, hospitals, trunk roads, rivers, protected areas. 70,148 of them have no Wikipedia article in any language describing that place. A mapper can point to each one on the ground; no encyclopedia can tell you anything about it.

Two different gaps, kept apart. 73,341 features carry no wikidata or wikipedia tag, but a missing tag only means nobody has done the linking, which is a job for mappers. The number in the headline is the stronger one: every untagged feature was matched by position and name against this project’s corpus, every item of which has an article by construction, so a feature with no match within two kilometres is one no Wikipedia covers.

The headline

Named features in OSM

93,272

across 12 classes, villages to rivers

Nothing found at all

70,148

no item, no article, no match within two kilometres

Item but no article

19,431

Wikidata holds it, no Wikipedia in any language writes it up

Described already

3,689

of 93,272 named features; the other 21.4% carry some Wikimedia tag

These are two jobs, not one. The features that are described already but untagged need a mapper to add one tag. The features with no article need somebody to write one, and most of them are villages and schools that no encyclopedia has ever had a reason to cover. Only the second is a content gap in the sense the rest of this project means it.

Bars are features with nothing found at all. Villages dominate by an order of magnitude, which is what you would expect: OSM maps every settlement it can reach, and an encyclopedia has never had a reason to describe most of them.

What to write about

The features with no article anywhere. Roads and rivers first within each class, by how many OSM ways carry the name, which is the closest thing here to a length. Names link to OSM, coordinates to the spot on the map.

67,342 more are omitted here: the bulk classes are sampled at 60 each because a table of every unmatched Ugandan village would be a twenty-megabyte page. Every row is in data/ug_osm_undocumented.csv, which is where this page stops being a summary and becomes a worklist.

Tagged one way but not the other

19,625 features carry one of the two tags and not its partner, overwhelmingly Uganda's schools, which were imported into OSM with item references en masse. The cheapest fix on this page: the identifier is already there and the matching tag is a single edit. The first 60 of them:

Where this comes from. One Overpass query per class of feature over the Uganda admin boundary, asking for tags and a centre point rather than full geometry. Only named features count: an unnamed one cannot be documented in an encyclopedia anyway. Roads and rivers arrive as many OSM ways per route, so linear features are grouped by name.

How the matching works, and why not by name. A first attempt asked Wikidata for each name together with country=Uganda and found almost nothing, for two reasons that both matter: “Gulu” also names places in Indonesia and Nigeria, and Gulu in Uganda carries no country statement at all, so the filter rejected the very item it should have found. The match is therefore geographic: within two kilometres of a corpus item that shares a name word. Every corpus item has at least one article by construction, so a match means the place is described somewhere.

What the numbers are not. “No article found” is a search result, not a proof of absence: a place whose article sits under a different name, or whose Wikidata item carries no coordinates, will read as absent. Nor does this page claim those places have no Wikidata item, only no article; Uganda has 58,240 Wikidata items with no article in any language, and some of these will be among them. The segment count correlates with length but does not measure it: a road split finely scores higher than a longer road split coarsely.

Rebuild. python src_data/osm_features.py, then python src_viz/export_data.py and python src_viz/build_pages.py osm. The fetch checkpoints per class, so an interrupted run resumes rather than starting over, and three Overpass mirrors are tried in turn because the public instances hand out 429s and 504s freely. Full exports are in data/ug_osm_features.csv and data/ug_osm_undocumented.csv.
